title: Distiller output — the contract between judgement and assembly
description: Distillers judge; tools assemble. A distiller never writes a role file: it emits claims, and the assembler decides which slice each one lands in, writes the frontmatter, regenerates the index and merges the citation graph. Same claims in, byte-identical tree out — which is what makes a drain reviewable as a content diff.

telemetry.description: Density is size-invariant by construction, and this is how that is checked: a ratio that jumps an order of magnitude against history is an alarm for review, never a quota to hit.

claims.description: An empty array is a correct output. A drain that admits nothing has found nothing that clears the bar.

class.description: The epistemic class. These decay and verify differently: domain against the field, solution against the tree, intersection against the governing decisions, rationale until it is promoted to an ADR.

topic.description: Slice key. Claims sharing a topic land in the same slice; a slice that outgrows its budget splits.

title.description: A one-line statement of the finding, not a topic label. Distillers naturally write these as claims ('X causes Y, and the cost is Z'), which is exactly what makes a useful retrieval cue in the index.

body.description: Prose, with inline citations where the source carried them. Written to be read by whoever holds the role.

evidence.description: Observation content hashes supporting the claim. The rubric asks for at least two independent observations, or one decision-type observation.

merge_target.description: Existing slice/section this claim strengthens rather than adds to. Preferring a merge over an addition is what keeps a long-lived role file dense instead of merely long.

shared_with.description: Other roles that own this claim. Two or more owners route it to a shared slice, so the knowledge lives once and cannot drift between copies.

observed_at.description: When the fact was written, YYYY-MM-DD — the memory's own modified stamp, else the file's mtime. Rendered at the foot of the section so two divergent sections on one topic read in time order.

allOf.$comment: Domain-only evidence comes from a sibling project: it is transferable knowledge about a FIELD, never a statement about this repository. Filed as `solution` it asserts what this system implements; as `workflow` or `rationale` it asserts how this team works. tools/fabric/assembler/intake.py enforces this in code as well, because lint's fallback validator cannot evaluate a conditional when jsonschema is absent.
